newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE backs Kuwait's defence rights.
newsitem.headline: UAE backs Kuwait's defence rights.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates on Wednesday said it backed Kuwait's right to defend itself, the official WAM news agency reported.
It quoted Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Sheikh Hamdan bin Zaid al-Nahayan as saying the UAE backs Kuwait and "its keeness (to safeguard) its security and stability."

He was speaking after a meeting with Kuwaiti Defence Minister Sheikh Ahmad Hamoud al-Jaber al-Sabah who was on a whirlwind tour of the Gulf to rally support among 1991 Gulf War allies for a fresh U.S. military buildup in the region.
Kuwait on Monday agreed to receive more U.S. soldiers and stressed it would not hesitate to take further measures to deter what its sees as threats by former occupier Iraq.
Skeikh Ahmad later traveled to Oman on the final leg of his tour of Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries.

The GCC is an economic, political and military alliance which groups Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman and the UAE. He has already visited regional heavyweight Saudi Arabia, the island state of Bahrain and Qatar.
